tagline.text: A southwest Cebu town of coral-stone church, Spanish watchtower and tiered waterfalls

location.label: Location
location.text: Southwest coast of Cebu Island facing the Tañon Strait, Samboan municipality (15 barangays)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800~2,500 (bus from Cebu City, local transport and snacks; lodging not included)

children.text: Samboan is a Tañon Strait coastal town about 150km south of Cebu City. The coral-stone Church of St. Michael the Archangel, what is described as the tallest and best-preserved Spanish watchtower in Cebu, and the 147-step Jacob's Ladder all sit on one hill, while tiered waterfalls such as Aguinid Falls lie inland.

Samboan sits at the southwestern tip of Cebu Island, looking out over the Tañon Strait. It borders Ginatilan to the north, Oslob to the east and Santander to the south, and Wikipedia gives its 2024 population as about 20,000 across 15 barangays. It lies about
150km
south of Cebu City, so it is awkward to squeeze into an itinerary built around whale shark encounters in Oslob or Kawasan Falls, and that distance keeps it quiet with few visitors.

The heart of town is the Church of St. Michael the Archangel on a hilltop. It is known as one of the oldest Spanish-built churches in Cebu, made of coral stone, and is designated a national protected heritage structure. Wikipedia says the town was founded in 1784, and one Cebu tourism guide says the church was built in 1842. The three-story coral-stone watchtower (Campanario de Antigua) was built to watch for Moro raiders and is considered the tallest and best-preserved watchtower in Cebu.
The 147 steps linking the church to the coast are known as Jacob's Ladder (Escala de Jacobe). The stone stairway is said to date from 1878, and from the plateau about

above sea level the Tañon Strait opens out in front of you. Inland you will find Aguinid Falls, Da-o Falls and Hidden Falls, and the Colase Marine Sanctuary offers snorkeling and diving. Rather than trying to see everything in one go, spend half a day on the church hill and another half on the waterfalls.

Besides the church and waterfalls, there is more to explore on foot. Ponong Lake in the town center is a brackish lagoon of about 1 hectare and about 3 m deep, described as good for birdwatching, and Mt. Bartolina, on the border of Barangay Bulangsuran and Canang in Oslob, is called the highest peak in southern Cebu, with views of the sea on both sides of the island. You ride a motorcycle taxi for about 15 minutes and finish on a narrow footpath. Near Calatagan there are small caves with narrow entrances you have to crawl through, but signage is poor, so go with a local guide. Most of the prices and transport details in this guide come from local tourism write-ups and blogs, and for many entrance fees and exact schedules I could not find an official source. I have marked those as "check locally", so ask the municipal tourism office or your accommodation before you go.

blocks.title: Church of St. Michael the Archangel

children.text: A coral-stone church on a hilltop plateau in the middle of town. It keeps details such as pilasters, an arched entrance and a relief of the Spanish royal seal, and is designated a national protected heritage structure. A town festival honoring St. Michael is held around September 29 each year.

A three-story Spanish coral-stone watchtower said to have been built to watch for Moro raiders. Many guides call it the tallest and best-preserved watchtower in Cebu. From the top floor you can see the island and the sea together.
A 147-step stone stairway up to the plateau by the church. It is said to have been built in 1878, and the Tañon Strait widens out as you climb.
A five-tier waterfall in Barangay Tangbo, easy to reach because it is only about

off the national highway. You can walk up the shallow, slippery rock bed to the upper tiers, which makes it a good place for casual swimming. After rain the water rises and becomes dangerous, so avoid it on wet days. There are no special facilities around the falls, so bring water and snacks.
A waterfall in Barangay Suba, described as the highest in Samboan. One guide gives its drop as about 90 feet (about
). After a hill walk you follow the stream up a steep, narrow path, so sturdy shoes are essential.
A hidden waterfall in Barangay Bonbon, also called Triple Drop because the water falls in three streams. Guides say you ride a motorcycle for about
10 minutes
from Tangbo and then walk about
15 minutes
across a stream.
A marine sanctuary managed jointly by the town and a fisherfolk group, where you can snorkel and dive. A fee is said to apply, but the amount could not be confirmed, so check locally.

blocks.title: Samboan Museum and San Sebastian stone walls

children.text: The Samboan Museum, housed in the former municipal hall, displays artifacts of local life. Old stone walls also survive in the San Sebastian area behind the church, which are worth a slow walk through the lanes.
Take a Samboan-bound bus from the Cebu South Bus Terminal. Reported travel times vary, but it is safest to allow about
4–5 hours
by bus.
Get off in Barangay Tangbo and head to Aguinid Falls. You can walk in from the highway and climb the shallow rock bed to the upper tiers.
Move to the town center for lunch. Try local sweets such as Samboan cookies and tortas.
Look around the Church of St. Michael the Archangel, then climb toward Jacob's Ladder and the watchtower.
Enjoy the view of the strait from the top of the watchtower and come back down. Be sure to check the last bus back before service ends.

Buses are not frequent, so a day trip is tight. If you are short on time, combine Samboan with Oslob or Moalboal and make it two days, one night. After swimming at a waterfall, keep a spare set of clothes and a towel in your bag to stay comfortable on the bus.

items.title: Two days, one night
items.subtitle: Waterfall exploring and the marine sanctuary

children.text: Arrive in Samboan, drop your bags and stroll slowly around the church, watchtower and Jacob's Ladder.
Swim at Aguinid Falls or Hidden Falls, then have dinner at a town eatery.
Snorkel at the Colase Marine Sanctuary or trek to Da-o Falls.
After lunch, take a bus toward Cebu City or Oslob.
Choose which waterfalls to visit based on the weather. After heavy rain the streams are dangerous.
A direct flight from Manila (MNL) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
From the airport, take a taxi or Grab to the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City.
Flight schedules and fares change with the season and airline.
Board a Samboan-bound bus at the Cebu South Bus Terminal. The distance is about
150km
, and one transport-guide site lists the trip as about
5 hours
and the fare as about
The number of buses differs between sources, so check the last departure at the terminal and the last bus back from Samboan.
Some guides also mention about
3 hours
by taxi or chartered vehicle.
You can walk to the church and watchtower in the town center. Use tricycles or motorcycle taxis (habal-habal) for the waterfalls and outlying barangays.
Some waterfall access roads are narrow and rough, and motorcycle taxi drivers often guide you along the way.

You can visit Samboan year-round, but the dry season is best for waterfall swimming and for walking the church and watchtower. In the rainy season the streams can swell and make waterfall access dangerous.
Around September 29, the feast of St. Michael brings a town festival that is busier than usual but lively. It is wise to check lodging ahead of time then.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Waterfalls are steady and the walk up the church hill is most comfortable.
Good for sea and waterfall swimming, but the midday sun is strong. See the church late in the afternoon.
Rainy season, with possible storms and typhoons
Waterfalls can swell and become dangerous, and the St. Michael festival is held in late September.

Samboan does not have many large resorts; small guesthouses and resorts are scattered along the coast. During high season or festivals it is safer to book ahead. To see both the waterfalls and the church in one trip, staying in the town center or near Tangbo is the most convenient. Samboan is a long way from Cebu City for a day trip, but if you stay overnight you can walk the church hill with almost nobody around in the morning light.

Local sweets such as Samboan cookies, Torta Especial and Torta de Tangbo are mentioned in guides. Seafood is often grilled from the day's catch at seaside eateries. Some eateries have short hours, so check ahead before a late lunch.
In the evening, take a slow walk along the coast. There are no large stores or malls, so it helps to bring snacks, water and basic medicine from Cebu City.
Buses leave from the Cebu South Bus Terminal in Cebu City; check the last bus back from Samboan as soon as you arrive.
Visit the church and watchtower in early morning or late afternoon rather than midday, when it is cooler and photos look better.
Jacob's Ladder has 147 steps, so wear shoes with good grip rather than flip-flops.
Waterfall routes are rough and cross streams, so you will want water shoes and a waterproof bag.
Some waterfall areas have weak phone signal, so download offline maps.
Bring plenty of cash. In a small town ATMs may be scarce.
Keep quiet during Mass at the church and take photos in a way that does not disturb the service.
It is close to Oslob, famous for whale shark encounters, so you can easily combine the two on one trip.
If you want to see several waterfalls, it is easier to negotiate a motorcycle taxi by the half day, and agree on the fare before you set off.
The church interior may not be open outside Mass times, so ask locals about its opening hours.
Streams below the waterfalls can rise suddenly on rainy days and right after rain, so do not go into the waterfalls.
The rocks at the falls are very slippery. Do not climb steep spots like Da-o Falls alone; go with a local guide.
Parts of the watchtower and stairs have low or no railings, so hold children's hands as you climb.
Fares and bus times can change. Check locally before you set off.
In the marine sanctuary, do not step on or touch the coral.
The church and watchtower are protected heritage sites, so do not write on the walls or take stones away.
Samboan's eastern neighbor, known for whale shark encounters and its Spanish-era heritage district.
A diving base reached by heading north along the west coast. It pairs well with Samboan in one trip.
A signature waterfall of southwestern Cebu, famous for canyoneering and swimming.
The hub city where you catch the bus to Samboan, with the south bus terminal.
